## Review Question
 
This map was developed as part of a scoping review to answer the question:
 
*"How is artificial intelligence (AI) used, validated, governed, and implemented responsibly in evidence synthesis, and what are the perceptions and levels of trust regarding its use?"*
 
## Evidence Map Framework
 
The evidence gap map plots the stages of the evidence synthesis process (e.g., search strategy development, title and abstract screening, full-text screening, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment) against key outcome domains related to AI in evidence synthesis.
 
The outcome domains were identified based on the review objectives and include:
 
- Performance, efficiency, and usability of AI in evidence synthesis
- Responsible use of AI in evidence synthesis
- Perceptions, acceptability, and trust regarding the use of AI in evidence synthesis
 
## Eligibility Criteria
 
Articles that were preprints, books, conference proceedings, conference abstracts, conference posters, narrative reviews, literature reviews, published before 2015, or not available in English or French were excluded.
 
## Search Strategy
 
The initial search was run on **19 February 2026** in:
 
- MEDLINE
- Scopus
- Embase
- Compendex
 
## Screening and Mapping
 
Relevance screening and data mapping were conducted using a human-in-the-loop approach that combined human reviewers with DistillerSR's AI tools, including DistillerSR's Artificial Intelligence System (DAISY) and Smart Evidence Extraction (SEE).
 
All final inclusion and exclusion decisions, as well as evidence mapping decisions, remained subject to human reviewer oversight, validation, and reconciliation procedures.
 
All screening was conducted in DistillerSR, and EPPI-Mapper was used to produce the final evidence gap map.
 
## Living Updates
 
This map will be updated approximately every 6 months, with the next search being run in October 2026.
